How the planner would be split up, and why two files is not enough

Where: Nothing you can see. This is about how your planner is stored behind the scenes — one record today, several after. No control, no screen, no setting changes.

your words, kept in full — one line per thing you said

first said number 3. i don't want to see the storage, I don't think professional apps have that. and for that one how will you sepaarate the files, I think one for the inside notes and one for everything would work great righ?

the cause, measured, and how I fix it

The storage bar is dropped. You are right — no ordinary app shows you a fullness gauge, and it was my idea rather than yours. Gone.

On splitting the files: your instinct is correct, and it gets most of the way there. Notes are the weight. Pulling them out drops everything else to 8% of its limit, which is solved for good.

But I measured your actual notes, and one of them changes the answer:

notesizeshare of all your notes
"App update ideas"637.7 KB93%
your other 71 notes, together47.8 KB7%

So a single notes file would be 67% full on day one, and 93% of it is one note. That note is 629,292 characters — it is a real working document, not a mistake. Keep writing in it and the notes file hits the same wall the planner is heading for now.

The fix is the same idea as yours, taken one step further:

one record per task  → 72 records, biggest 40 KB ✓
a long note gets its own  → past a size limit, it splits again ✓
so nothing you can write can ever fill a single record

Adding tasks then adds records rather than filling one, and there is no ceiling to run into again.

What you would notice: nothing. Same planner, same screens. It would load in pieces rather than all at once, which on a large planner is faster, not slower.

The picture shows: ['every number measured from your 10 Sep export, not estimated', 'your two-file split: everything-else drops to 8%, notes land at 67%', 'one note - "App update ideas" - is 637.7 KB, 93% of all your notes', 'the storage bar is dropped at your word; nothing on screen changes']

Three things worth saying plainly.

  • This is the riskiest change we have discussed, and it is not urgent. It rewrites how every screen loads and saves. You are at 75% with 256 KB spare, so there is time to do it carefully rather than soon. I would ship the backups card first and come back to this.
  • I would do it in two steps, not one. First notes out of the main record — your idea, the bigger win, and the smaller change. Then a record per task once that is proven. Doing both at once means if anything goes wrong there are two suspects.
  • You cannot see this one working, which is unusual for this board. There is no screen to photograph. What I can show is the before and after of your real data, which is what the picture is, and a check that proves every task and every note still reads back identically after the split.

THE RULES OF THIS BOARD — permanent, they never come off

  1. The AFTER shows the SCENARIO you raised, not a tidy example. If you report a control at the bottom of a window, the pictures are OF a control at the bottom of that window — the BEFORE photographed in that exact state, the AFTER showing that same state fixed. A picture of the easy case proves nothing about the case you hit.
  2. EVERY change is drawn here and waits for your word — including a fix to a fix. Restated 2026-10-11 in your words: "from now on, show me on the PNG file before you do anything, then wait for my approval to put it in the demo." I had been treating a correction to something already approved as a continuation of that approval, and putting it straight on the demo. It is not. A new change is a new card, drawn, waiting, however small and however obviously right it looks to me.
  3. Minimax advises; I write the code. Changed 2026-10-11 on your instruction — "change the rules from Minimax from executioner of code to just co-brain only, I feel like a lot of the code stuff you are doing is going back and forth." Every change used to become a written brief, a round-trip and a verification step; on a one-line fix that was four steps, and its own verification was wrong three times in a row. It still advises on every turn — that part earns its place. The gate that enforced the old way is switched off, and kept so it can be switched back.
  4. When you ask to SEE it, you get a photograph of it working — not a drawing, and not the same drawing twice. A drawing is only ever a first look at something not built yet. The moment you ask again, I build it, test it and photograph the real thing. Added 2026-10-10, after I left two drawings on this board across three replies and you had to ask three times.
  5. I do not hand anything back half done. If a card says fixed, it is built, measured, gate-tested and photographed before you read the word. Added 2026-10-10, in your words: "your response must be complete and done before saying done".
  6. I find the pattern before I invent one. Before changing how anything looks, I find the control in the planner that already does that job and copy it. Added 2026-10-10, after I drew a new calendar when the app already had one, and after I changed a css rule that three controls share instead of the one you asked about. Both came from acting on what I expected instead of measuring what is there. When you ask "is that Claude or Minimax" — it is me. Minimax writes only the exact text I dictate.

  8. No code before you approve the card. You approve card by card. Only when you say “make it live” do I write anything.
